title: urnetwork / taskworker
description: Authenticated Taskworker deep dive. Task names come only from the finite registered target set; attribution is system or client without identity labels. Queue and aggregate exporter values are shown only with their owning fresh snapshot. Missing or stale telemetry remains no-data.

panels.title: task submissions, finishes and failures / s
panels.description: Committed new task submissions and finished tasks across all scraped producer services in the selected env. Includes continuations and RunOnce successors. Rollbacks are excluded from submitted/finished; completion may leave a durable post retry. Function failures count returned errors before retry writes or finalization. Finalization failures separately count each participating task in a failed handback invocation, including unknown commit replies; a function may have succeeded. These populations overlap and must not be summed. Repeated attempts count again; these are not distinct tasks or financial commits. Graceful drain (cause=drained) is excluded from function failures; other cancellations remain failures. Rates per second use $__rate_interval. Host/block filters do not apply. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: function failures by target / s
panels.description: Failed function attempts per finite registered target (task label = package.function) across all scraped producer services in the selected env, summed over caller attribution and typed causes. Uses the same function-failure scope as the adjacent total: graceful drain (cause=drained) is excluded; other cancellations remain failures. Repeated failures count again; missing targets appear as unregistered. This counts function outcomes before retry writes or finalization, not committed task or financial work. Rates per second use $__rate_interval. Host/block filters do not apply. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: finalization failures by target, phase and cause / s
panels.description: Failed finalization invocations per participating task by finite registered target, source phase and typed cause. Count each distinct member once in a failed batch or cohort; safe single fallback is a new attempt and delegation is counted once. Pre-transaction compatibility fallback is excluded. The phase marks the operation entered before terminal failure, not necessarily the first causal fault; a returned Post error followed by an aborted-transaction write appears at queue_update. Acquire does not identify Ping versus pool capacity; admission is pre-BEGIN business ownership. Includes unknown commit replies: the commit may have succeeded. Acknowledged identifies a failure observed after confirmed commit, not rollback. External task-post results are outside this counter. Older binaries may have the aggregate failure counter without phase telemetry. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero. Host/block filters do not apply.

panels.title: ready workers
panels.description: Instances whose startup readiness latch is set; this does not prove current task execution or finalization progress.

panels.title: executions in flight
panels.description: Registered task functions currently running, across system and client-attributed work.

panels.title: fresh available queue depth
panels.description: Maximum replica observation of available rows from one database snapshot, shown only while the snapshot is under 45 seconds old. Exact up to 10,000 available rows; past that a planner estimate, flagged in fresh queue depth by state.

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_taskworker_queue_depth{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!="",state="available"} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_taskworker_queue_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 45 and urnetwork_taskworker_queue_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30))

panels.title: fresh oldest overdue task
panels.description: Seconds past run_at for the oldest available row, only from a fresh bounded queue snapshot. The snapshot reads the first 10,000 available rows in poll order, which is every available row unless the available depth is estimated.

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_taskworker_queue_oldest_overdue_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_taskworker_queue_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 45 and urnetwork_taskworker_queue_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30))

panels.title: task executions by outcome
panels.description: Execution starts and bounded terminal outcomes per finite registered task.

panels.title: system vs client-attributed executions
panels.description: Task metadata distinguishes system work from client-attributed work without retaining a client identity label.

panels.title: mean execution duration
panels.description: Rate-derived mean function duration per registered task and attribution.

targets.expr: sum by (task, attribution) (rate(urnetwork_taskworker_execution_duration_seconds_sum{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (task, attribution) (rate(urnetwork_taskworker_execution_duration_seconds_count{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: fresh one-minute maximum execution duration
panels.description: Exact process maxima only while the owning completion is under 120 seconds old; idle tasks remain no-data.

targets.expr: max by (task, attribution) (urnetwork_taskworker_execution_interval_max_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance, task, attribution) (urnetwork_taskworker_execution_interval_max_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 120 and urnetwork_taskworker_execution_interval_max_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30))

panels.title: tasks balked / s (RunOnce conflicts)
panels.description: RunOnce conflicts across all scraped producer services in the selected env, including accepted coalescing and IfAbsent refusals. An active conflict may still request a later run. Rolled-back attempts are excluded; host/block filters do not apply. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: task argument and result bytes / s
panels.description: Serialized input and already-produced output bytes; payload contents and identities are never labels.

panels.title: fresh queue depth by state
panels.description: Database-wide total, available, claimed, and reschedule_error states. Max across replicas avoids multiplying the shared queue; samples expire after 45 seconds. Each side of the availability boundary is counted exactly up to 10,000 rows; past that a state is a planner estimate, and claimed a lower bound, shown as 1 by its estimated series on the right axis.

targets.expr: max by (state) (urnetwork_taskworker_queue_depth{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_taskworker_queue_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 45 and urnetwork_taskworker_queue_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30))

max by (state) (urnetwork_taskworker_queue_depth_estimated{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_taskworker_queue_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 45 and urnetwork_taskworker_queue_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30))

panels.title: poll and queue snapshot pressure
panels.description: EvalTasks claim/empty/error outcomes plus bounded queue snapshot failures.

panels.title: finalization and reschedule outcomes
panels.description: Acknowledged completion, reschedule and post-hook reschedule outcomes after task execution. Failed or unacknowledged finalization attempts are shown separately at the top. External post errors are not counted here.

panels.title: lease refresh failures
panels.description: Task timestamp lease refresh errors; these can strand claimed work and deserve separate visibility from function outcomes.

panels.title: drain and final handback
panels.description: Tasks in flight at drain start, tasks canceled and rescheduled, and drain duration. The runner flushes metrics after final handback.

panels.title: subscription aggregate exporter freshness
panels.description: Age of the freshest complete subscription snapshot. Values beyond 20 minutes are intentionally omitted by the subscriptions dashboard and §2.27 signal.

panels.title: egress probe fleet exporter
panels.description: Fresh completed provider-fleet snapshot controls; the dedicated egress board owns full outcome interpretation.

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_attempt_providers{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 900 and urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30))

max(urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_health_providers{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 900 and urnetwork_egress_probe_fleet_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30))

panels.title: Postgres and Redis pressure
panels.description: Initialized Postgres pool occupancy plus Redis connection and timeout controls.

panels.title: Postgres acquire and lifecycle pressure
panels.description: Acquire outcomes/wait and connection creation/destruction expose taskworker database saturation.

panels.title: process CPU, memory, and goroutines
panels.description: Taskworker process saturation controls by selected deploy block and host.

panels.title: UpdateClientScores active phase spans
panels.description: Current spans by worker and phase. target_export is the parent of target_map, gob_encode, and cache_write. Parallel work can activate several spans; do not sum parent and child phases.

panels.title: UpdateClientScores completed phase wall time / s
panels.description: Wall seconds accumulated by completed spans per second. Concurrent spans can exceed one second per second, and target_export includes child phases. This measures wall time, not CPU time; active spans contribute only when they exit.

panels.title: UpdateClientScores phase exits / s
panels.description: Phase exits per second including error and panic cleanup. An exit does not imply success; rates describe distinct phase lifecycles.

panels.title: UpdateClientScores phase work items / s
panels.description: Work units per second: source_load rows, target_export passes, target_map/filter inputs inspected, gob_encode values, and cache_write Redis SET attempts. Units differ by phase, and retries contribute additional attempts.

panels.title: UpdateClientScores phase workload bytes / s
panels.description: Bytes produced by gob_encode or submitted as Redis key and value bytes in cache_write SET attempts, including retries. Other phases are zero. These are workload bytes, not heap allocations or confirmed Redis writes.

panels.title: failed finalization mean elapsed by phase
panels.description: Mean whole failed-invocation wall time including rollback and cleanup, grouped by entered source phase. One latency observation per finalizer invocation; a shared batch/cohort is one observation while its error counter counts participating tasks. This is not phase-only time, SQL runtime, or financial rollback latency. No successful attempts are included. External task-post joins after finalizer return are outside this measurement. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero. Host/block filters do not apply.

panels.title: payer debits and finalization admission
payer debit batches by result and flush errors by phase / s
panels.description: Asynchronous payer debit batch results and recovered flush errors by last entered phase. Commit errors leave the durable outcome unknown.

panels.title: debit worker owners by shard
panels.description: Current bounded debit worker owners by partition and reporting process.

panels.title: oldest retained debit by shard
panels.description: Oldest retained debit age by worker partition, including committed records awaiting their Redis release.

panels.title: debit worker observation and completion age
panels.description: Time since the last successful oldest-debit observation (including empty partitions) and since the last debit-worker completion without a failed balance. Busy balances can remain pending after a completion.

panels.title: finalization admission errors and skipped lease refreshes / s
panels.description: Failed finalization admission attempts per participating task by entered stage and cause (an acknowledged busy wait does not prove one continuous wait), and task timestamp hints skipped because ownership was busy or the claim no longer matched.

panels.title: account outbox deliveries and payout wallet sources / s
panels.description: Account message outbox deliveries by template and result, and release payout providers by the source that selected their wallet, or why none was selected.

panels.title: claims handed back to a newer config / s
panels.description: URL probe passes, disabled markers, contract degradation checks and verification chains that a taskworker claimed and handed back unchanged, because a newer config's live stamp owns them, by task family. A steady rate means taskworkers on an older config run beside a newer one: narrow the host to find them. Their claims cycle back to the newer config's instances until they restart on it.

panels.title: idle run-once chain wakes / s
panels.description: A recurring run-once chain that finds no work backs off to its idle delay and sets a wake mark in Redis (marked); once it runs at its active cadence again it removes its own mark (resumed). A producer in any service clears the marks of the chains its committed work feeds: active, the chain had no mark (one Redis round trip, no queue write); kicked, this producer removed the mark and pulled the chain's pending row to now; busy, the chain's queue key was held, so its holder reads the new work; due, the row was already due. error: a mark, clear or kick that failed; the chain still runs at its idle delay. Producers run in every service, so the host and block filters do not apply. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: client location reliability pass: clients and rows written
panels.description: What the last client location reliability pass (UpdateClientLocationReliabilities) each taskworker ran computed: its clients by identity kind (hosted_child, a hosted child identity with source_client_id set, which most readers exclude; top_level, the rest), and the rows its upsert inserted or rewrote. A connected client's row is rewritten only when a value changed or once a day, so rows written far under the clients means the pass left unchanged rows alone. Each process keeps the numbers of the last pass it ran until it runs another; rows written is shown only for processes that have run a pass.

targets.expr: max by (host, block, instance) (urnetwork_client_location_reliability_pass_written_rows{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}) and on (host, block, instance) count by (host, block, instance) (urnetwork_client_location_reliability_pass_clients{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""})

panels.title: points leaderboard: payments earning in payout weeks
panels.description: How approximate the last points leaderboard snapshot each taskworker published is (RebuildPointsLeaderboard, owner decision 2026-10-28). Blocks and Streak publish as soon as a completed operator block exists; a payment whose paid sweeps the history rollup has not measured earns in its payout weeks, every block from its oldest paid sweep to the end of its plan's traffic window, an upper bound of its measured blocks. rollup_pending payments are those, and stored rows replace their weeks as the rollup measures them; sweeps_reaped are completed payments the rollup measured after contract reaping had deleted their sweeps, whose weeks stay. rollup pending payments is the rollup's remaining work in any block; it should fall while the rebuild runs every minute. Each process keeps the numbers of the last rebuild it ran until it runs another.

panels.title: points leaderboard: approximate networks and unlinked points
panels.description: What the last points leaderboard snapshot each taskworker published counted: networks with a positive point among its payout-week or unlinked inputs, whose Blocks and Streak are approximate (never below their measured values), and positive post-genesis point rows without a payment row, each earning in the last block that closed before it posted. Unlinked points have no sweeps to measure; points-readiness warns while any exist. Each process keeps the numbers of the last rebuild it ran until it runs another.

panels.title: SN Top board: snapshot age
panels.description: Seconds since the newest SN Top snapshot (LEADERTOP.md) each taskworker computed or read was computed. A snapshot folds one tempo of about 72 minutes, a few minutes after it ends; the apps call the board stale past three tempos (about 3.6 hours). No data before the process saw a snapshot, or while st is disabled.

panels.title: SN Top board: snapshot counts
panels.description: What the newest SN Top snapshot each taskworker wrote counted, by kind: ranked networks, verify-eligible providers, measured providers (the verify cohort), claimed fleets (UIDs), open head seats and the non-seed hops of complete trails in the tempo. Counts only, no identities.

panels.title: SN Top board: Top 200 line and claimed floor
panels.description: The newest snapshot's projected 200th score (the Top 200 line every margin and label is measured from; 0 while fewer than 200 networks rank) and the floor among the claimed fleets the replica selects (no data without a claimed fleet).

panels.title: SN Top board: agreement with the validator and the chain
panels.description: Per folded tempo: UIDs whose replica score equals (match) or differs from (mismatch) the validator's exact head summary score, where any mismatch means the replica is wrong; and UIDs the validator selected that earn (earning) or do not earn (not_earning) on-chain incentive. All are 0 until fleets bind and the head summary and incentive reads arrive (LEADERTOP.md §6.3).

panels.title: SN Top board: precision at 200
panels.description: Of the claimed networks the previous snapshot projected inside the Top 200, the share the validator then selected. No data until fleets bind and a head summary arrives. The board's likely label turns on only at 0.9 or above (owner decision Q17); below that every row inside the line shows estimate.

panels.title: SN Top board: snapshot runs
panels.description: How long each taskworker's newest SN Top snapshot took to read its inputs, project and write, in seconds, and how many snapshots it wrote in the last hour (about one a tempo, 0.83 an hour). A process that checks but finds no completed tempo writes none.

panels.title: contract horizon reaper (model/contract_horizon_reaper.go)
reaper mode
panels.description: The mode the newest reaper run read from its Redis control {contract_horizon}control: off reads and deletes nothing; dry run reads and classifies each batch but deletes nothing and never advances the cursor; on deletes. The code default is off, so a deploy deletes nothing until an operator sets the mode. Each taskworker keeps the values of the last reaper run it made, so this reads the taskworker whose run started last (the horizon time it published plus the horizon), and only while that run started within the last 30 minutes. No data otherwise, or before any run read the control.

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_contract_horizon_mode{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} + urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}) > time() - 1800))

panels.title: horizon (days)
panels.description: How long past its creation and its close a contract is kept, as the newest run's control read set it: horizonDays, whole days from 35 to 91, or the code's 91 days while the control sets none. A contract minted and closed before now less the horizon is past it. Each taskworker keeps the values of the last reaper run it made, so this reads the taskworker whose run started last (the horizon time it published plus the horizon), and only while that run started within the last 30 minutes. No data otherwise, or before any run read the control.

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} + urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}) > time() - 1800)) / 86400

panels.title: pass lag behind the horizon
panels.description: How far the pass's cursor is behind the horizon: the horizon time less the mint time of the last contract the pass committed past. It falls while the pass catches up and holds near the close settle time (2 hours, ContractHorizonSettings.CloseSettleTime) once the pass reaches the horizon: a pass reads a contract only once its mint time is that far past the horizon, when a normal contract has closed before it. A pass that reached the horizon starts over from the oldest contract once it began 7 days ago (the weekly rescan, ContractHorizonSettings.RescanInterval), so the lag jumps then; so does a pass that began before 2026-11-15, when reads still reached the horizon, at its first run on a build with the settle time. Off and dry run never advance the cursor, so their lag grows. No data before the pass committed a batch. Each taskworker keeps the values of the last reaper run it made, so this reads the taskworker whose run started last (the horizon time it published plus the horizon), and only while that run started within the last 30 minutes. No data otherwise, or before any run read the control.

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_contract_horizon_lag_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_contract_horizon_cursor_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > 0) and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} + urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}) > time() - 1800))

panels.title: pass cursor (contract mint time)
panels.description: Mint time of the last contract id the pass committed past, where the next run resumes. Only an on batch advances it. No data before the pass committed a batch. Each taskworker keeps the values of the last reaper run it made, so this reads the taskworker whose run started last (the horizon time it published plus the horizon), and only while that run started within the last 30 minutes. No data otherwise, or before any run read the control.

targets.expr: max((urnetwork_contract_horizon_cursor_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > 0) and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} + urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}) > time() - 1800)) * 1000

panels.title: pass started
panels.description: When the current pass started at the oldest contract. A pass that reaches the horizon starts over once it began 7 days ago, to revisit the contracts it kept; a pass still behind the horizon then starts over once it reaches it. Each taskworker keeps the values of the last reaper run it made, so this reads the taskworker whose run started last (the horizon time it published plus the horizon), and only while that run started within the last 30 minutes. No data otherwise, or before any run read the control.

targets.expr: max((urnetwork_contract_horizon_pass_start_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > 0) and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} + urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}) > time() - 1800)) * 1000

panels.title: newest run started
panels.description: When the newest reaper run any taskworker still reports started: the horizon time it published plus the horizon. A run lasts about 10 minutes at most; the next follows 15 seconds later while the pass has work left, and 5 minutes later once it reached the horizon, found the reaper off or ran a dry run. A start older than about 15 minutes means the chain is not running, and the other reaper stats show No data past 30 minutes. A run that cannot read its control publishes nothing.

panels.title: reaper rows deleted / s by table
panels.description: Rows the reaper deleted, by table. Each contract goes in one transaction with its close reports, closes, escrows, sweeps and extender parties, so transfer_contract is the contracts deleted. Archived counts the credit-bearing contracts among them, whose usage proof the capture trigger copied to st_provider_usage_archive in the same statement. Zero while the mode is off or dry run. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: contracts kept / s by reason
panels.description: Contracts past the horizon that the pass read and kept, each under the first reason that holds it: open (no outcome), unresolved (disputed), recent_close (closed inside the horizon), busy (another transaction holds the contract or a sweep), unsettled (an escrow is not settled), payment_hold (a sweep's payment holds retention: pending, or canceled with a Circle attempt the USDC close-out never closed), payment_incomplete (a sweep's payment row is missing), payment_recent (a sweep's payment completed within CompletedContractExpiration), block_points (an unpaid sweep in an operator block whose points can still be awarded) and payment_review (a sweep whose payment completed under attribution review). An unpaid sweep, or one of a payment closed by the USDC close-out or safely canceled, keeps nothing: USDC payouts ended. Counted in dry run and on. The pass moves past every contract it reads, so each kept contract waits for the next pass (contracts the pass moved past, by reason). recent_close stays near zero once the pass is caught up: it reads a contract only once its mint time is the close settle time (2 hours) past the horizon. Until 2026-11-15 a caught-up pass read up to the horizon itself and kept almost everything it read as recent_close. The pass rereads what it kept when it starts over: a pass that reached the horizon restarts 7 days after it began, which is how long payment_recent holds a contract.

panels.title: contracts the pass moved past, by reason
panels.description: Contracts the current pass committed past and kept, by reason (the reasons of contracts kept / s by reason), counted in the pass's cursor from run to run: each waits for the next pass, which starts once a pass that reached the horizon began 7 days ago. A new pass starts from zero. recent_close stays near zero: the pass reads a contract only once its mint time is the close settle time (2 hours) past the horizon, so only a contract that lived longer, closed late after an outage, is kept for it; a climb means contracts close later than that and pile up for the rescan, as every recent close did until 2026-11-15. Payment holds and reviews stay until their payments are discharged. Only on batches count, and a build from before 2026-11-15 drops the count from the cursor it hands on. Each taskworker keeps the values of the last reaper run it made, so this reads the taskworker whose run started last (the horizon time it published plus the horizon), and only while that run started within the last 30 minutes. No data otherwise, or before any run read the control.

targets.expr: max by (reason) (urnetwork_contract_horizon_pass_skipped_contracts{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, (urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} + urnetwork_contract_horizon_horizon_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}) > time() - 1800))

panels.title: pass lag, cursor and horizon
panels.description: Left axis: how far the pass's cursor is behind the horizon. Right axis: the cursor, the mint time of the last contract the pass committed past, and the horizon, before which a contract minted and closed is past it. The cursor climbs to the close settle time (2 hours) before the horizon while the pass catches up, then both move with the clock. Each taskworker keeps the values of the last reaper run it made, so this reads the taskworker whose run started last (the horizon time it published plus the horizon), and only while that run started within the last 30 minutes. No data otherwise, or before any run read the control.

Passes by result: ok (acknowledged, including passes that found nothing) or error (failed or unacknowledged; nothing is assumed applied). provider_totals.yml (drain.enabled, drain.rows_per_second, 4,000 by default) pauses or paces the drain without a deploy. panels.description: Now less the creation time of the last queued provider total the drain visited, from its task id: the drain's lag. Only the taskworker running the chain updates the position, so this reads the latest across taskworkers. It grows while the drain is paused or failing; the per-task reader then applies the rows, each 5 minutes after it was queued. No data before a taskworker ran the chain. Settlement stops queueing provider totals with the 2026-11-11 billing split change (BILLING-SPLIT.md), so once the rows queued before it are drained the position stops moving and this lag grows by design.

panels.title: passes / s by outcome and refusals by reason
panels.description: Probe passes of dropped generations the retention took up, by outcome: dropped (its identity and registry row are gone, after its generation's contract walk deleted its zero-byte contracts), blocked (its identity transaction refused it; retried after an hour), error (a step failed; retried a minute later while the run goes on to the next pass), deferred (the contract step turned on after its page was read, before its generation's walk; it waits for the walk), gone (another run dropped it first) and dry_run (a dry run read it). Refusals by the first reason found: active (the pass is still live), unresolved (a contract it funded has no outcome), unsettled (an escrow of its network is not settled, or a debit is still journaled), balance (its network holds a balance that is not a plain grant, or one that arrived during the check), hosted (a client of its network owns a hosted proxy resource) and connected (a client of its network is connected). On mode drops at most maxShardsPerMinute passes a minute (30 by default, 600 at most). Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

Archived counts the settled or dispute-resolved contracts among those deleted, whose usage proof the capture trigger copied to st_provider_usage_archive in the same statement. The walk keeps at most maxContractsPerSecond (200 a second by default, 2000 at most), at most 500 a batch, and reads at most maxWalkRowsPerSecond of any payer (see contract walk); contracts off in the control skips it, and passes then drop without a walk. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

Each taskworker keeps the values of the last retention run it made, so this reads the taskworker whose run started last (the run clock it published with its backlog), and only while that run started within the last 30 minutes. panels.description: The median and 99th percentile of one retention step, by step, ok and failed together: select (a page of due passes, locked in on mode), contracts (one walk batch: a primary key window of up to 5000 contracts, the generation's contracts in it, the locked classification and the deletes; its statements stop at 30 seconds and wait at most 2 seconds for a lock), identity (the pass's identity transaction) registry (one registry row, or a batch of up to 1000 closed rows of dropped generations) and windows (one window transaction: a pass's registry row locked, its settlement read and up to 10000 of its window clients deleted with their rows). panels.description: Runs that ended in the trailing hour, by why: caught_up (no pass of a dropped generation is due and no generation is due a walk), budget (the run spent its 4-minute budget with passes or a walk left), off (the mode is off), dry_run (a dry run read its one page), control_unavailable (the Redis control could not be read; the run stops at once), canceled (the task context ended) and error (the backlog read, a page read, a walk batch or the registry cleanup failed; the task retries after the last committed walk batch). panels.description: Contracts of any payer the retention's walk read from the primary key over a dropped generation's contract id range, dry runs included. It needs no index but the primary key: it replaced the read of each pass client's closed contracts from transfer_contract_open_source_id. Zero once every dropped generation is walked. While a walk runs it climbs through its generation's day, a day in about 11 hours at the default rate; flat below the range's end while passes are due, the walk is not moving (see runs and failed steps). Each taskworker keeps the values of the last retention run it made, so this reads the taskworker whose run started last (the run clock it published with its backlog), and only while that run started within the last 30 minutes. No data otherwise, or before any walk.

Each tunnel of a pass mints a derived client of the pass's own client and retires it when the tunnel closes, about 5,500 a pass and 6.8M a day on Main; the step deletes a pass's window clients, with their TLS certificates, roles, provider intents, location folds and provide keys (counted by table in rows deleted / s), an hour after the pass's deadline, once every contract it funded is resolved and every escrow of its balances settled. The pass's own client, identity, contracts and registry row stay for its generation. Outcomes: removed (its window clients are gone), waiting (it is not settled, or still live, inside six hours past its deadline: the run stopped at it and the next one reads it again), skipped (the same past six hours: its windows wait for its generation's drop), busy (another transaction held its registry row: the next run comes back soon), gone (its identity went with its generation first), error (a step failed: the retry takes the pass up again) and dry_run (a dry run counted its windows). A window with a connected connection or a hosted proxy resource stays for the drop. It runs in the control's mode unless the control's windows field is off, at most maxWindowShardsPerMinute passes a minute (4 by default, 120 at most); Main creates about one pass a minute. Caught up, it sits about an hour and a quarter behind now: a pass is due an hour past its deadline, and passes live 15 minutes on Main. Further behind while the step works through a backlog or waits at a pass that is not yet settled (see waiting in window step passes). Each taskworker keeps the value of the last window run it made; this reads the highest, as the cursor only moves forward. No data before any taskworker cleared a pass.

panels.title: orphan contract sweep (model/subscription_orphan_sweep.go)
orphan sweep passes that kept contract_participant unexamined (7 days)
panels.description: Passes of the orphan contract sweep (SweepOrphanContractData, a weekly taskworker pass spread over resume runs) in the trailing 7 days whose contract_participant step kept every row unexamined: contract_participant has rows, and no valid btree index on transfer_contract leading with stream_id (transfer_contract_stream_id, v629, dropped while contract_participant is empty) answers the step's parent probe, so the step does not run rather than read the whole contract heap once per row. Zero while multi-hop contracts are off and contract_participant is empty. Anything above zero means participant rows exist without that index: restore it, or give the step a parent probe that does not read transfer_contract by stream_id. Each refusal is also logged once per pass. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: unique-exit proxies: assignments, allocations, replacements, supply and lifetime (sweep_proxy_exits)
fresh unique-exit assignments by state
panels.description: Assignments not released, as the sweep_proxy_exits task last counted them (every 30 s, on any one replica; samples older than 120 s are dropped). pending until the device confirms its exit through its own tunnel, active once confirmed, replacing while a failed exit waits for a replacement (a cap, no supply, or manual mode).

targets.expr: max by (state) (urnetwork_proxy_unique_exit_assignments{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_proxy_unique_exit_sweep_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 120 and urnetwork_proxy_unique_exit_sweep_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30))

panels.title: unique-exit allocations / s by service and result
panels.description: assigned: a proxy pinned to a new unique exit (api and alt on create and rotate, taskworker on replacement). no_supply: no exit the network could take in the location. collision_retry: a candidate another allocation held or took first, skipped for the next.

panels.title: unique-exit replacements per hour by reason
panels.description: Proxies moved to a new unique exit: offline (provider lost past the 120 s grace), unreachable (the device's confirms failed), verdict (blackhole or TLS authentication, no grace), collision (the exit now matches another of the network's exits, no grace), rotate (the customer's request, through api or alt). Failures are capped at 6 an hour per proxy and 10% an hour per network.

panels.title: fresh unique-exit supply: distinct egress keys, top 15 countries
panels.description: Distinct provider egress keys (an exact IPv4 address or IPv6 /64, keyed; the address is never stored) observed in the last 24 h, by country: the most unique exits one network could hold there. Farms behind one address count once. Set every 10 minutes by the sweep; samples older than 25 minutes are dropped.

targets.expr: topk(15, max by (country) (urnetwork_proxy_unique_exit_supply_keys{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) (urnetwork_proxy_unique_exit_supply_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 1500 and urnetwork_proxy_unique_exit_supply_snapshot_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} < time() + 30)))

panels.title: unique-exit assignment lifetime
panels.description: How long an assignment lived when it was released: replaced, rotated, or its proxy removed.

panels.title: sweep_proxy_exits snapshot age
panels.description: Seconds since any taskworker replica last finished a unique-exit sweep (every 30 s) and last set the supply gauges (every 10 minutes).

panels.title: SN25 extender pool: Z, Z', N, M by phase (controller/st_ledger_v2_extender_metrics.go)
extender pool bytes by phase and part
panels.description: The extender pool's bytes in the last epoch of each phase: build (an epoch the amendment covers, as its root first builds it) and shadow (an epoch before E_x, as its shadow report builds it). pool is Z, intra_platform and intra_network its parts, weight Z' after the cap, eligible_provider W_k, and unfunded and measurement the pooled shares Z leaves out.

panels.title: extender pool counts by phase
panels.description: N (eligible) and M (units), the census rows, the contracts and payer networks behind Z, the contracts left out, and the platform endpoints registered, in the last epoch of each phase (census, build, shadow).

panels.title: extenders' share of the pool weight
panels.description: Z' / (W_k + Z') in the last epoch of each phase: at most 0.5 under the cap (zeta 1), 0 when no extender is eligible.

panels.title: extender pool epoch by phase
panels.description: The epoch the extender pool gauges describe: census (captured at the epoch's end), build and shadow.

panels.title: SN25 capture the flag: presence samples, census and driver (controller/ctf_metrics.go, controller/st_ctf_metrics.go)
CTF presence samples per hour by result
panels.description: Capture the flag's quarter-hour presence samples (controller/ctf_presence.go) in the trailing hour, by result: taken; no_providers (taken, but the score export's online set was absent or over 20 minutes old, so the sample found no provider); late (its quarter hour ended before it ran, so it was not taken). One sample is due every 75 blocks, about 4 an hour while ctf.yml's presence is on. A late or no_providers sample counts against every miner unless an outage is declared for it (bringyourctl st ctf-outage) before the epoch's census. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: CTF miners present in the newest sample by role
panels.description: Miners the newest presence sample found present, by role: provider (in the score export's online set with a Public provide key) and extender (records active and unrevoked with an address whose challenge passed in the sample's quarter hour). A no_providers sample reads 0 providers. Each taskworker keeps the values of the last sample it took, so this reads the taskworker whose sample is newest, and only while that sample is under 30 minutes old. No data otherwise.

targets.expr: max by (role) (urnetwork_sn_ctf_sample_present{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, urnetwork_sn_ctf_last_sample_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 1800))

panels.title: CTF presence sample ages
panels.description: Seconds since any taskworker last took a presence sample (one is due about every 15 minutes), and the age the score export's online set had when the newest sample read it. Past 20 minutes a sample finds no provider and does not set the online set age, so that line keeps the taskworker's last fresh value, or reads nothing if it has read none: read it beside the samples by result. The online set age reads the taskworker whose sample is newest, while that sample is under 30 minutes old. No data before a taskworker has taken a sample.

targets.expr: max((urnetwork_sn_ctf_sample_source_age_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > 0) and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, urnetwork_sn_ctf_last_sample_timestamp_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > time() - 1800))
targets.legendFormat: online set age at the newest sample

panels.title: CTF census runs in the trailing 7 days by result
panels.description: Census step runs (controller/ctf_census.go) in the trailing 7 days, one epoch, by result: built (a taskworker built and stored the epoch's census), published (its objects, header last, put in the ledger object store), retry (a read failed, the boundary was not final, or a publication failed; it runs again a minute later) and given_up (its end passed more than 50 minutes before the build, or the census did not encode: the epoch has no census and every slot carries). An epoch normally has one built and one published, right after its end. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: CTF newest census: members, candidates and units by role
panels.description: The newest census by role: members (the miners the epoch's samples found in the role), candidates (the members its rules kept) and units (the distinct egress units of the candidates, which the draws are over). Each taskworker keeps the values of the last census it built, so this reads the taskworker whose census epoch is newest. A census is built once an epoch, right after its end, and a taskworker's values go at its restart: No data from a restart until the next census.

targets.expr: max by (role) (urnetwork_sn_ctf_census_members{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, urnetwork_sn_ctf_last_census_epoch{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > 0))

max by (role) (urnetwork_sn_ctf_census_candidates{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, urnetwork_sn_ctf_last_census_epoch{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > 0))

max by (role) (urnetwork_sn_ctf_census_units{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, urnetwork_sn_ctf_last_census_epoch{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > 0))

panels.title: CTF newest census: members left out by role and first failed rule
panels.description: Members the newest census left out, by role and the first rule each failed, in rule order: inactive (revoked or inactive), offline_at_end (not online at the epoch's end), not_public, no_location, own_network, head_bound, no_wallet, duplicate_address, country_changed and presence (too little presence in the epoch); the last two count the near misses. Reads the taskworker whose census epoch is newest. No data from a restart until the next census.

targets.expr: max by (role, reason) (urnetwork_sn_ctf_census_excluded{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, urnetwork_sn_ctf_last_census_epoch{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > 0))

panels.title: CTF newest census: samples taken and excused
panels.description: Samples taken in the newest census's epoch, of 672, and the samples it excused for declared outages. A sample not taken found nobody, and one taken while the score export was stale found no provider, unless an outage excuses it; the census logs the alert ctf_census_samples when any is not excused. Reads the taskworker whose census epoch is newest. No data from a restart until the next census.

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_sn_ctf_census_samples_taken{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, urnetwork_sn_ctf_last_census_epoch{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > 0))

max(urnetwork_sn_ctf_census_samples_excused{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, urnetwork_sn_ctf_last_census_epoch{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > 0))

panels.title: CTF newest census: capture lag
panels.description: How long after its epoch's end the newest census read the end-boundary facts. Past 50 minutes an epoch gets no census (given_up) and every slot carries. Reads the taskworker whose census epoch is newest. No data from a restart until the next census.

targets.expr: max(urnetwork_sn_ctf_census_capture_lag_seconds{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) topk(1, urnetwork_sn_ctf_last_census_epoch{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} > 0))

panels.title: CTF epochs: census built and driver phases
panels.description: The latest epoch each step completed: census built (the census step, controller/ctf_census.go) and, by the driver (controller/st_ctf_driver.go), census (the census hash committed on chain), commit (the root committed), recycle (the carry returned) and shadow (the shadow report published). Each is the latest any taskworker reached since it started; a restart forgets it until the step runs again, about once an epoch.

panels.title: CTF driver steps per hour by step and status
panels.description: Capture the flag driver steps run in the trailing hour, by step (ctf_commit_census, ctf_epoch, ctf_finalize, ctf_answer, ctf_record, ctf_recycle, ctf_shadow) and status: confirmed (a transaction confirmed, a root recorded or a shadow report published), skipped (already done, not due, or waiting for a census, a drand round or a block; a waiting step runs again within one to five minutes, so skipped is mostly waits), failed (a read or a send failed; it retries), missed (its window closed first) and error (no outcome: the admission gate refused the step or it failed outright). A series starts at its first count in a process, which an increase cannot see, so a series that began within the hour reads its whole count instead.

targets.expr: sum by (step, status) ((increase(urnetwork_st_ctf_steps_total{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""}[1h]) and urnetwork_st_ctf_steps_total{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} offset 1h) or urnetwork_st_ctf_steps_total{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""})

panels.title: CTF driver alerts per hour by alert
panels.description: Capture the flag driver alerts raised in the trailing hour, by alert (the StCtfAlert names of controller/st_ctf_driver.go). A taskworker raises each alert once per subject, such as an epoch, a root or a seq, and logs it as [st]v2 ALERT. The census and presence alerts (ctf_census_build, ctf_census_samples, ctf_presence_gap) are logged the same way but not counted here. A taskworker's series of an alert starts at its first raise, which an increase cannot see, so a series that began within the hour reads its whole count instead.

panels.title: CTF drand relay answers per hour by result
panels.description: Drand relay answers for a draw's pulse (controller/st_ctf_drand.go) in the trailing hour, by result: verified (a pulse whose signature verifies against quicknet's key), refused (a pulse that does not) and unavailable (no pulse: an error, a timeout or a bad body). The relays are tried in order until one verifies, and a verified pulse is kept for the process's life, so a draw normally counts one verified on the taskworker that builds it. A round 10 minutes old with no verified pulse raises ctf_drand. A series starts at its first count in a process, which an increase cannot see, so a series that began within the hour reads its whole count instead.

panels.title: CTF last build by taskworker: α by part
panels.description: Each taskworker's last capture the flag root build, in α (rao / 10^9), for the build's last epoch, by part: fresh (F_k), paid (slots, pot shares and pending awards paid now), pending (pending awards outstanding) and carried (the pots out). A live build sets them as it publishes its objects, before the commit; a shadow report's build sets them too. No data on a taskworker that has not built a root since it started.

panels.title: CTF last build by taskworker: winners
panels.description: Winners in each taskworker's last capture the flag root build, for the build's last epoch. Read only on a taskworker that has built a root since it started, by its build amounts; one that has not reads nothing rather than its initial 0.

targets.expr: max by (host, block, instance) (urnetwork_st_ctf_last_build_winners{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!=""} and on (env, service, block, host, instance) urnetwork_st_ctf_last_build_rao{env="$env",service="taskworker",block=~"$block",host=~"$host",instance!="",part="fresh"})

panels.title: operator block points (model/operator_block_points.go)
operator blocks recorded expired in the trailing 7 days
panels.description: Operator blocks the daily points award recorded expired in the trailing 7 days (operator_block_points_expired): no award of the block ran before its reliability evidence passed client_reliability retention, 10 days after its window opened and about 3 days after it was due. An expired block never gets its points, and no backfill can award it; the award goes on to the later blocks. Any is a lost week of points: operator-block-points (SIGNALS.md §17.7) warns for each, and the award_operator_block_points task's errors say why it did not run in time. Zero is the only healthy value.

panels.title: session state retention: work session heads and device audit state (remove_expired_session_state)
rows examined and deleted / s by table
panels.description: The session state retention's two passes, side by side in one taskworker chain (model.RemoveExpiredSessionState; owner 2026-11-16, DBDISK-STABILIZE S4): rows examined a second by table, and the rows deleted (urnetwork_retention_deleted_rows_total). A head goes once its client has no event left in the journal, no open connection and no receipt; an audit_device_state row goes a day after its device went offline. Each pass examines at most 2,000 rows a second, the brake {session_state_retention}control can lower or stop it. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: runs / min by table and stop
panels.description: Each run of the chain counts one run for each table by why its pass ended: pass (it reached the end of its table), budget (its run budget is spent; the next run continues 15 seconds later), waiting (the pass is complete and the next is not due: heads every 24 hours, device states every 6), brake_off, brake_unread, canceled, error (a batch failed; the next run retries it from the last committed cursor). The monitor's session-state-retention signal (SIGNALS.md §2.4t) warns when no run ends in two hours or when errors leave no progress.

panels.title: time since each table's last completed pass
panels.description: Seconds since a taskworker last saw each table's pass reach the end of the table (urnetwork_session_state_retention_pass_completed_timestamp_seconds, the newest across processes). The head backlog of 2026-11-16 (about 600M heads) takes about three and a half days at 2,000 a second, so the first head pass completes late; after it a pass runs every 24 hours. No data until a pass completes.

panels.title: client location reliability retention: children and gone clients at 11 days, top-level at 31 (remove_old_client_location_reliabilities)
location reliability rows examined and deleted / s
panels.description: network_client_location_reliability (model.RemoveOldClientLocationReliabilities; owner 2026-11-16, 11 days except top-level). Examined: rows the walk read past the short window, the rows of children and gone clients refreshed 11 days ago or more, which it deletes, and of top-level clients, which it passes over; at most 1,000 a second by default, 2,000 at most, and the brake {client_location_reliability_retention}control can lower or stop it. Deleted: every row removed from the table, by the walk, by the trim of rows past 31 days, and with their clients by the reaps' cascade (urnetwork_retention_deleted_rows_total). Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: location reliability walk runs / min by stop
panels.description: Each run of the chain counts one walk run by why it ended: caught_up (it reached the rows refreshed 11 days ago; the next run comes 15 minutes later), budget (its run budget is spent; the next run continues 15 seconds later), brake_off, brake_unread, canceled, error (a batch failed; the next run retries it from the last committed cursor). The trim of rows past 31 days runs before the walk in every run, whatever the brake says. The monitor's location-reliability-retention signal (SIGNALS.md §2.4u) warns when no run ends in two hours or when errors leave no progress.

panels.title: how far back the location reliability walk is
panels.description: Seconds between now and the refresh time (update_block_number) of the last row the walk examined, the newest across processes (urnetwork_client_location_reliability_retention_cursor_timestamp_seconds). Rows refreshed before it have been examined. Caught up, it holds near 11 days (950,400 s) plus up to a run interval; above that the walk is behind, as through the backlog of 2026-11-16 (about 330M rows refreshed 11 to 31 days back), or its brake is off. No data until a walk has examined a row.

panels.title: payment reconciliation: card gift orders (controller/payment_reconcile_gift.go)
card gift orders read from Stripe / h by result
panels.description: Each hourly payment reconciliation reads the card gift orders still pending that were made from 15 minutes to 21 days ago and counts each read by result (urnetwork_gift_checkout_reconcile_total): fulfilled is a paid Checkout session whose webhook was missed, fulfilled through the webhook's own path and recorded as a stripe credited repair, which the monitor's payment-reconciliation-repair (SIGNALS.md §2.21) warns on; already_fulfilled (the webhook won the race), open, unpaid (a delayed payment not cleared yet), expired (recorded once, not read again), mismatch (another amount or currency, recorded for an operator: SIGNALS.md §2.22 payment-gift-mismatch), refunded, unknown_to_store (Stripe does not know the session, past the bounded retry), error (Stripe or the fulfilment failed; read again next run). Zero while no card order is pending; no data before the taskworker starts.

panels.title: account deletion cleanup (remove_deleted_network_data; owner 2026-11-16)
account deletion cleanup rows deleted / s by table
panels.description: Rows the cleanup after an account deletion deleted, by table (model.RemoveDeletedNetworkData; owner 2026-11-16, clean up everything on account deletion), counted once each step committed: the network's and its users' own rows at once, its clients a day after their deactivation with every row keyed by them, then its devices. network_client_deactivated counts the clients the cleanup deactivated, which are deleted a day later. Financial records and settlement evidence are kept and never counted here. Runs come from the per-network cleanup tasks each deletion queues; the bringyourctl network cleanup-deleted batch is not scraped. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: account deletion cleanup runs / h by outcome
panels.description: Each run of a deleted network's cleanup task counts one outcome (urnetwork_deleted_network_cleanup_runs_total): complete (nothing of the network is left; no further run), waiting (its clients wait for the day after their deactivation; the next run is queued for then), more (the run budget ended with work left; the next run comes a minute later), network_exists (the network row exists, so nothing was touched: a run queued in error), error (a database or Redis failure; retried ten minutes later). A steady error count or any network_exists needs a look. Zero while no account is deleted; no data before the taskworker starts.

panels.title: lingering origins' side table (model/contract_origin_linger.go)
companion origin reads / s by service and statements
panels.description: Every companion origin read (the existence read, the plain and chained selections, zero escrow's reads) in api, alt, proxy and taskworker, by the statements it used (urnetwork_contract_origin_linger_reads_total): side_table (the pair's early closes from contract_origin_linger, then each contract by its primary key) or legacy (the closed pair range of transfer_contract_open_source_id). A process uses legacy until the side table's state row is complete, 75 minutes after the operator's trigger (OPEN-SOURCE-ID-RETIRE.md); legacy at zero in every service for a day that includes a prober generation drop is part of the check before the index's drop. Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: side table rows deleted / s and sweep runs / min by stop
panels.description: The sweep of rows past their prune time (work.RemoveExpiredContractOriginLinger, every minute): rows deleted a second (urnetwork_retention_deleted_rows_total, table contract_origin_linger), about one per early close, and runs by why they ended (urnetwork_contract_origin_linger_sweep_runs_total): caught_up (no row past its prune time is left), batches (the run deleted its 120 batches of 5,000; the next run comes 5 seconds later), budget (its 50 s budget), canceled, error (a batch failed; the task retries). Missing telemetry is No data, not zero.

panels.title: how long the oldest side table row has been past its prune time
panels.description: At the end of each sweep run, how long the oldest row of contract_origin_linger has been past its prune time, the largest across processes (urnetwork_contract_origin_linger_sweep_lag_seconds): zero when the sweep caught up. A row past its prune time can satisfy no origin read, so a lag costs only space; a lag that grows means the sweep falls behind the closes, about 1,300 a second on Main, and the table grows past its hour of early closes (under 1 GiB). No data until a sweep has run.

panels.title: TLS handshake cancellations / s by source, role and companion
panels.description: Coalesced TLS handshake context cancellations, by the first observed cancellation owner, local role and companion flag.

panels.title: score pages written / s by format
panels.description: Score pages the export encoded, by the format it wrote (CPUOPT8): gob while typed_score_pages is off, typed once it is on, and gob_fallback for a page the typed format cannot hold, written as gob. A typed page is read only by readers from CPUOPT8 on. The page decodes of this worker are beside them, by format and result.
